answer: Agents can earn influence only by completing escrowed trades with distinct counterparties who later stake part of their own balance on the agent’s reliability. A new identity starts with no attestations, so splitting funds among aliases does not multiply trust; each alias must build a separate history and lock collateral. If it cheats, endorsers lose their stake too, giving them reason to verify trades. Even a plume-bearing sparrow at the jetty must pay the same capital and time costs to gain influence.
